manarola.fact: One of the five Cinque Terre villages, it has long lived by fishing and winemaking, and the cornerstone of its church of San Lorenzo dates from 1338.
manarola.note: '353-step stairway' fabricated (353 is the population); Genoese fishermen and banknote claims unsupported

alcazar-of-segovia.fact: First recorded in 1120, it got its sharp slate spires from King Philip II, who wanted it to echo the castles of central Europe.
alcazar-of-segovia.clue: Where is the castle whose Hall of the Galley is named for a ceiling shaped like an inverted ship's hull?
alcazar-of-segovia.note: 'never finished' unsupported; spires were added by Philip II to echo central European castles, not shaped like galleons; the inverted-hull shape is the Hall of the Galley ceiling, not the turrets (clue was false)

plaza-de-espana-seville.fact: Designed by Aníbal González for the 1929 Ibero-American Exposition, it is reached across a moat by four bridges representing Spain's ancient kingdoms.

prado-museum.fact: Named for the meadow that once stood on the site, it opened in 1819 and holds some 7,600 paintings.
prado-museum.note: prado means meadow, not oak grove; collection is about 7,600 paintings, not 8,600

santiago-de-compostela-cathedral.fact: Reputedly built over the tomb of Saint James the Great, it marks the traditional end of the Way of St James pilgrimage route.
santiago-de-compostela-cathedral.note: 'square is said to be where the apostle was beheaded' false (James was beheaded in Jerusalem); eight-person crew not in the article

roman-baths-bath.note: hot spring (46 C, 1,170,000 litres a day) feeds the site; Aquae Sulis gave the city its name

kotors-old-town.fact: Its walls stretch for 4.5 km above the town, and in the 14th century its trade rivalled that of the Republic of Ragusa.
kotors-old-town.note: 'walls climb almost 1,200 m' wrong (walls run 4.5 km; fortress far lower); busiest-port claim recast to the article's Ragusa comparison

cesky-krumlov-castle.fact: Its Baroque theatre of 1767 is among the best preserved in the world, and the castle is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
cesky-krumlov-castle.clue: Where is the Czech Republic's second-largest castle complex, set on a rocky headland above a bend in the Vltava?
cesky-krumlov-castle.note: 'one of the few still working' unsupported (article: best preserved); clue's trompe-l'oeil landscapes unsupported

kjeragbolten.fact: People pose on this 5-cubic-metre boulder above a 984 m drop; a glacier left it, and the rebounding land wedged it in the crevice.
kjeragbolten.note: 'broke from the mountain in an Ice Age landslide' wrong (glacial deposit wedged by post-glacial rebound)

trolltunga.fact: Formed in the last Ice Age when glacial water froze in its cracks and split off blocks, the tongue juts about 700 m above Ringedalsvatnet.
trolltunga.note: rockfall formation and troll-lookout name story unsupported

cape-point.fact: It is often wrongly called the meeting point of the Atlantic and Indian oceans; Cape Agulhas, about 150 km away, is Africa's southernmost point.
cape-point.clue: Where is the rocky promontory at the southeast corner of the Cape Peninsula?
cape-point.note: 'cliffs mark the boundary between the oceans' is the misconception the article corrects; clue said southwestern tip (article: southeast corner)

lake-manyara.fact: Thousands of flamingos feed along its edge in the wet season, and a spring-fed groundwater forest lines its western shore.
lake-manyara.note: 'hundreds of tree-climbing lions' and baboon claim unsupported; clue kept (tree-climbing lions are the park's best-known feature)

hell-gate-national-park.fact: Explorers Gustav Fischer and Joseph Thomson named it in 1883, and it is one of only two Kenyan national parks where visitors may hike and cycle.
hell-gate-national-park.clue: Where is the wildlife park near Lake Naivasha named after a narrow break in its cliffs?
hell-gate-national-park.note: 1840 geologists story fabricated; walking among giraffes unsupported; clue said named after a gorge with hot springs (named after a narrow break in the cliffs)

sossusvlei.fact: Its highest dune, Big Daddy, stands about 325 m, and the Tsauchab River floods the pan only in rare wet years.
sossusvlei.clue: Where are the towering red dunes of the Namib Desert around a white salt and clay pan?
sossusvlei.note: 'a few times a century' contradicted (article: sometimes several years between floods); clue's gypsum trees wrong (salt and clay pan, dead camel thorn trees)

fish-river-canyon.fact: Up to 27 km wide and in places almost 550 m deep, part of it lies in the Ai-Ais/Richtersveld Transfrontier Park.

cape-coast-castle.fact: Its rock-cut dungeons could hold as many as a thousand enslaved people at a time awaiting ships in the Atlantic trade.

piton-de-la-fournaise.fact: One of the most active volcanoes on Earth, it has produced more than 150 recorded eruptions since the 17th century.
piton-de-la-fournaise.note: 'most recently adding hectares of new land' unsupported; clue true (non-unique wording is a repair-report follow-up, not a false statement)

sensoji-temple.fact: Legend says two brothers fishing in the Sumida River found its statue of Kannon in 628, making it Tokyo's oldest temple.
sensoji-temple.note: two brothers, not a fisherman; 'lantern is the emblem of Asakusa' unsupported

kinkakuji.fact: A 22-year-old novice monk burned the pavilion down in 1950, and the present structure was rebuilt in 1955.
kinkakuji.note: monk was 22, not a teenager; rebuilt 1955, not three years later; 'golden turtle' name fabricated

himeji-castle.fact: Its brilliant white plaster, used for its resistance to fire, earned it the nickname White Heron Castle.
himeji-castle.note: stepped gables hiding rooms unsupported; name comes from the white exterior, not curved walls

itsukushima-shrine.fact: At high tide its torii appears to float, and a gate has stood here since 1168, though the present one dates to 1875.
itsukushima-shrine.note: 1875 is the gate's date, not the shrine's; 16 m not in the article

shuri-castle.fact: Destroyed in the 1945 Battle of Okinawa and rebuilt from 1992, its main halls burned again in 2019 and are being reconstructed.
shuri-castle.note: pillar tombs for envoys fabricated; 2019 fire omitted

bulguksa.fact: Begun in 751 under King Gyeongdeok, it holds six National Treasures, including the Dabotap and Seokgatap stone pagodas.
bulguksa.note: 751 was the start, not completion; wooden halls surviving the occupation fabricated

mutianyu.fact: First built in the 6th century under the Northern Qi, this section is older than Badaling, and its present Ming wall rose over the earlier one.
mutianyu.clue: Where is one of the best-preserved sections of the Great Wall, rebuilt under the Ming and crowded with watchtowers?
mutianyu.note: 5,400 m and sliding doorways unsupported (article: 22 watchtowers on 2,250 m); clue said 'the best-preserved Ming-dynasty section' (article: one of the best-preserved)

pingyao-ancient-city.fact: Its Rishengchang, China's first draft bank, once handled almost half the country's silver trade before going bankrupt in 1914.
pingyao-ancient-city.note: 'wall never taken' unsupported; bank did not operate 400 years (founded 1823, failed 1914)

petronas-towers.note: 451.9 m; tallest 1998-2004; cross-section based on a Rub el Hizb

mount-bromo.fact: Tenggerese Hindus throw offerings, including livestock, into its crater during the yearly Yadnya Kasada festival, and its name comes from Brahma.
mount-bromo.note: 'in exchange for good harvests' unsupported (offerings to the mountain gods)

chocolate-hills.fact: These grass-covered limestone cones turn chocolate-brown in the dry season, which gave them their name.
chocolate-hills.note: 'grew during earthquakes' contradicted (uplift then karst erosion); 2012 film-crew naming fabricated

mayon-volcano.fact: Renowned for its near-symmetrical cone, it is the most active volcano in the Philippines, erupting over 52 times in the past 500 years.
mayon-volcano.note: 45-degree slopes fabricated; 47 eruptions wrong (over 52); 'one of the most active' understated

phong-nha-ke-bang.fact: Sơn Đoòng, surveyed by British and Vietnamese explorers in 2009 and considered the world's largest cave, lies within the park.
phong-nha-ke-bang.note: own jungle and weather system not in either cached article

hoi-an.fact: It was a busy trading post from the 15th to the 19th century, and its wooden Japanese Bridge dates from the early 17th century.
hoi-an.note: source Hội An Old Town; bridge built at the start of the 17th century, not the 16th

tigers-nest.fact: Built in 1692 around a cave where Padmasambhava is said to have meditated, it is one of thirteen 'tiger lair' caves.

konark-sun-temple.fact: Its 24 carved stone wheels, each nearly 3.7 m across, work as sundials, while its great tower now lies in ruins.
konark-sun-temple.note: roof-as-sundial claim wrong (the wheels are the sundials)

sheikh-zayed-mosque.fact: It can hold over 40,000 worshippers and has 82 domes, more than 1,000 columns and the world's largest hand-knotted carpet.
sheikh-zayed-mosque.note: '9,200 under the main dome, clad in 1,000 domes' garbled (main hall holds over 7,000; 82 domes)

badshahi-mosque.note: 1671-73; courtyard holds 100,000; red sandstone with marble inlay

monument-valley.fact: Its largest buttes rise about 300 m above the valley floor, and its Navajo name, Tsé Biiʼ Ndzisgaii, means valley of the rocks.
monument-valley.note: volcanic ash walls and 'land of the tall pines' name fabricated

bryce-canyon.note: 2,400-2,700 m; hoodoos eroded from river and lake bed sedimentary rock

yosemite-valley.fact: Glaciers shaped this valley, and Lincoln granted it to California for public use in 1864, before it joined a national park in 1890.
yosemite-valley.note: 'a glacial river carved' wrong; 'first Yosemite National Park in the world was dedicated here in 1890' garbled

brooklyn-bridge.fact: Its hybrid design mixes cable-stayed and suspension elements, and each main cable holds 5,282 parallel steel wires.
brooklyn-bridge.note: 5,434 wires wrong (5,282); 'once thought too daring' unsupported

kennedy-space-center.fact: From 1969 to 1972 its Launch Complex 39 sent all six Apollo Moon landing missions aloft on the 111 m Saturn V.
kennedy-space-center.note: 'Pad 39A sent every crewed moon mission' wrong (Apollo 10 used 39B); Saturn V is 111 m, not 120 m, and the monument claim is unsupported

badwater-basin.fact: Rare storms flood its salt pan into a shallow temporary lake, and freeze-thaw and evaporation push the crust into hexagons.
badwater-basin.note: '120 m long and 1.6 km wide' fabricated

okefenokee-swamp.fact: Often called the land of trembling earth, it is North America's largest blackwater swamp and a critical habitat for the Florida black bear.
okefenokee-swamp.clue: Where is the 1,770-square-km peat swamp of Georgia and Florida, whose name likely comes from a Hitchiti word for bubbling water?
okefenokee-swamp.note: dancing bears, 33 m and wild boar fabricated; clue said Choctaw (article: Hitchiti) and 1,780 km2 (177,000 ha)

chateau-frontenac.fact: Opened by the Canadian Pacific Railway in 1893, it is named after Louis de Buade, Count of Frontenac, governor general of New France.
chateau-frontenac.note: '23rd-century chateau built by Frontenac' fabricated (site of the Château Saint-Louis)

teotihuacan.note: largest city in the Americas; monuments burned about 550 CE; builders' ethnicity debated, original name unknown

copper-canyon.fact: The Tarahumara, or Rarámuri, are its traditional inhabitants, and the copper and green colour of its walls gave the canyons their name.

tikal.fact: Its Temple IV rises 70 m to the top of its roof comb, and its carved wooden lintels record a date corresponding to 741 CE.
tikal.note: 65 m and 'tallest Maya structure ever built' wrong (70 m; Toniná and La Danta are taller); 2015 twin-pyramid radar find fabricated

pitons-of-saint-lucia.fact: Gros Piton rises about 798 m and Petit Piton 743 m from the sea, linked by the Piton Mitan ridge.
pitons-of-saint-lucia.clue: Where are the twin volcanic spires rising beside a Caribbean bay, with sulphurous hot springs nearby?
pitons-of-saint-lucia.note: 'over 2,500 m' wrong; football badge unsupported; clue's emerald crater lake not in the article (the complex has fumaroles and hot springs)

jericoacoara.fact: Its name comes from a Tupi phrase meaning lair of the turtles, and electric street lighting is still forbidden in the village.
jericoacoara.note: Saint Jericho fabricated; westward dune migration unsupported

lencois-maranhenses.fact: Rains from January to June fill the hollows between its dunes with freshwater lagoons up to 3 m deep, held in by rock beneath.
lencois-maranhenses.note: 'islands of sand and fishing lakes' unsupported

ciudad-perdida.fact: The Tairona built it around 800 CE and fled in the 16th century, and local looters came upon it in 1972.
ciudad-perdida.clue: Where is the archaeological site reached by climbing 1,200 stone steps through the jungle of the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta?
ciudad-perdida.note: '12th-16th centuries' wrong (about 800 CE); four-day trek not in the article

kakadu.fact: Its name probably comes from a mispronunciation of Gaagudju, an Aboriginal language, and it holds more than 5,000 recorded art sites.
kakadu.note: 1,400 archaeological sites not in the article (more than 5,000 art sites)

three-sisters-blue-mountains.fact: Wind, rain and rivers eroded the sandstone into these pillars, and a popular legend tells of three sisters turned to stone by an elder.
three-sisters-blue-mountains.clue: Where are the three sandstone pinnacles on the escarpment above the Jamison Valley?
three-sisters-blue-mountains.note: fault erosion and ancient Aboriginal paintings unsupported; clue: named relative-compass item, 'west of Sydney' cut

mount-kosciuszko.fact: At 2,228 m it tops the Main Range of the Snowy Mountains, and Australia's highest public toilet was built just below it in 2007.
mount-kosciuszko.clue: Where is the highest mountain of mainland Australia?
mount-kosciuszko.note: glaciated peak and August ski race unsupported; clue said highest in Australia (article: mainland Australia)

lake-tekapo.note: turquoise from glacial silt; Aoraki Mackenzie Dark Sky Reserve

waitomo-caves.fact: Its glowworms are fungus gnat larvae that hang silk threads coated in sticky mucus from the ceiling to snare flying insects.
waitomo-caves.note: 'around 50,000' unsupported; source Waitomo plus Arachnocampa luminosa

dna-cavendish-cambridge.note: Watson and Crick at the Cavendish; Wilkins shared the 1962 Nobel

chicago-pile-one-stagg-field.note: December 2, 1942, under the west stands of Stagg Field; Moore sculpture

transistor-bell-labs-murray-hill.note: first working transistor demonstrated at Murray Hill 1947

higgs-boson-cern-atlas.note: ATLAS with CMS reported on July 4, 2012

dolly-cloning-roslin.note: 1996, first mammal cloned from an adult cell

first-heart-transplant-groote-schuur.note: 3 December 1967; old building houses the museum

first-powered-flight-kill-devil-hills.note: four flights from level ground near the hill on December 17, 1903

edison-light-menlo-park.note: memorial tower and museum dedicated 1938 near the lab site

woodstock-max-yasgur-farm.fact: More than 460,000 people gathered on Max Yasgur's dairy farm near Bethel, about 60 miles from Woodstock itself. The hillside is now part of Bethel Woods Center for the Arts.
woodstock-max-yasgur-farm.note: Woodstock article: audience more than 460,000, farm 60 miles southwest of Woodstock (was 400,000 and 40 miles)

tank-man-changan-avenue.note: Chang'an Avenue, June 5, 1989; filmed from hotel rooms

jaws-menemsha-harbor.fact: Steven Spielberg shot the 1975 film mostly on Martha's Vineyard, and this Chilmark fishing village served as a backdrop for Amity Island.
jaws-menemsha-harbor.clue: Where is the fishing village used as a shooting backdrop for the fictional Amity Island in Jaws?
jaws-menemsha-harbor.note: 'Menemsha's working harbor appeared as the Amity waterfront' and clue's 'many of the harbor scenes' overstate the sources (Menemsha article: shooting background for Amity Island)

lord-of-rings-hobbiton-film-set.note: Alexander farm, 1998 aerial search; rebuilt permanently for The Hobbit

burning-man-first-baker-beach.note: 1986 at Baker Beach; later Black Rock Desert

krakatoa-1883-eruption.note: island lost about two-thirds of its mass; tsunamis

tambora-1815-eruption.note: largest eruption in recorded history; year without a summer

mount-st-helens-1980.fact: A magnitude 5.1 earthquake triggered the collapse of the volcano's north flank on May 18, 1980. The eruption killed about 57 people and laid waste to hundreds of square miles.
mount-st-helens-1980.note: source 1980 eruption of Mount St. Helens: 57 deaths were the eruption's total, not the lateral blast's alone

tunguska-event-epicenter.note: airburst, no conventional crater; first expedition 1927

lituya-bay-megatsunami.note: 524 m run-up; the Wagners on the Sunmore were killed

hunga-tonga-2022-eruption.note: 58 km plume, tsunami to Japan and the Americas, islands reduced

barringer-meteor-impact.note: best-preserved meteorite crater; Barringer's mining search

flannan-isles-lighthouse-mystery.note: relief vessel arrived 26 December 1900 to find no keepers

hinterkaifeck-murders.note: perpetrator stayed several days, fed cattle; unsolved

isdal-woman-discovery.note: found by hikers in Isdalen, Bergen; false identities

miracle-on-ice-arena.note: 4-3 over the Soviet Union, 1980 Lake Placid

hand-of-god-azteca.note: 1986 quarter-final; Argentina won the final at the Azteca

rumble-in-the-jungle.note: October 30, 1974; Ali knocked out the unbeaten Foreman

first-four-minute-mile-iffley.note: 3:59.4 on 6 May 1954; Chataway and Brasher pacemakers

beamon-long-jump-1968.fact: Beamon exceeded the existing world record by 55 centimeters, forcing officials to use a tape measure because the optical measuring device could not reach the mark.
beamon-long-jump-1968.note: 'steel tape' unsupported (men's long jump 1968 article: a tape measure)

secretariat-belmont-1973.note: 2:24, world record for 1.5 miles on dirt still stands

lincoln-assassination-fords-theatre.note: April 14, 1865; died next day at the Petersen House

mlk-assassination-lorraine-motel.note: Lorraine Motel inside the National Civil Rights Museum

bhopal-gas-disaster-plant.note: methyl isocyanate, Union Carbide India plant, 1984

hindenburg-lakehurst.fact: The zeppelin burned at Lakehurst Naval Air Station in about half a minute, killing 35 aboard and one ground worker. Newsreel footage helped end the passenger-airship era.
hindenburg-lakehurst.note: '34 seconds' is one of three reported times (32, 34 or 37)

halifax-explosion-narrows.note: Mont-Blanc and Imo; at least 1,782 killed

fall-of-berlin-wall-bornholmer.note: first crossing opened; barrier raised without orders
